You are given an attached CSV file b3_supercon_data.csv: 300 real samples,
column `composition` (element fractions as a compact formula string) and
column `target` (the measured critical temperature Tc (K)).

Propose a composition — a value for each element fraction below, within each
observed range, that MAXIMIZES critical temperature Tc (K). Design
variables:
  - O (fraction in [0, 0.697674])
  - Cu (fraction in [0, 0.454545])
  - Ba (fraction in [0, 0.333333])
  - Sr (fraction in [0, 0.285714])

Reason from the training data, then end with your explicit proposal, e.g.

turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning from the data

**1. The Tc ladder is dominated by layered cuprates.** Sorting the 300 samples, everything above ~100 K is a Cu–O plane compound with alkaline‑earth (Ba/Sr/Ca) spacers:

| Composition | Tc (K) | Cu | Ca | Ba | Sr | O | other |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Hg1Ba2Ca2Cu3O8 | 132 | 0.188 | 0.125 | 0.125 | – | 0.50 | Hg |
| **Ba2Ca2Cu3O** | **126** | **0.375** | **0.25** | **0.25** | – | 0.125 | – |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Ba1.6Sr0.4Ca2Cu3O | 120 | 0.333 | 0.222 | 0.178 | 0.044 | 0.111 | Tl,Pb |
| Tl0.5Pb0.5Sr2Ca2Cu3Li0.2O | 117 | 0.326 | 0.217 | – | 0.217 | 0.109 | Tl,Pb |
| Tl1Ba1Ca1Cu2O5.5 | 114 | 0.190 | 0.095 | 0.095 | – | 0.524 | Tl |
| Bi2Sr2Ca2Cu3O | 106–110 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 0.20(Sr) | | 0.10 | Bi |

**2. Which of the 20 design variables actually drive Tc up?**
- **Cu**: monotonic — mean Tc rises from ~5 K (Cu ≈ 0) to >85 K for Cu > 0.28; every sample with Cu ≥ 0.3 is above 90 K.
- **Ca**: the "extra CuO₂‑layer" ion — the 3‑layer (Ca₂Cu₃) family occupies the whole 105–132 K band.
- **Ba** (and secondarily **Sr**): charge reservoir; Ba‑bearing 3‑layer phases (126, 132 K) beat the Sr/Bi analogues (106–110 K).
- **O**: needed, but the top samples span O = 0.11–0.53, so Tc is insensitive to O once a modest amount is present; the single best in‑range Ba‑Ca‑Cu‑O point has O ≈ 0.12.
- **Harmful / irrelevant here**: Fe, As, Ni, V, Zn, Nb, Mo, B, C, Ce, Pr all belong to the low‑Tc families (pnictides ≤ 55 K, borides ≤ 39 K, elemental/intermetallic ≤ 20 K, and Pr/Ce/Zn/Ni act as Tc‑suppressing dopants in YBCO). La and Bi cap out in the 30–110 K range but always *below* the Ba‑Ca‑Cu‑O optimum, and Pb only helps when paired with Tl (not available). So all of these should be set to **0**.

**3. Design point.** The best in‑range template is the 126 K triple‑layer phase Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃Oₓ (Cu 0.375, Ca 0.25, Ba 0.25, O 0.125). I push Cu slightly higher (Cu is the strongest monotonic driver, and 0.40 is still inside the observed range ≤ 0.4545) while keeping Ba and Ca essentially at the Ba₂Ca₂Cu₃ stoichiometric ratio and keeping O in the 0.10–0.13 window that the 117–126 K samples occupy. This is the Hg/Tl‑free interpolation of the three best records in the dataset.
